name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention and accurately describes a class-promotion data-table accessor returning a 2-byte entry pointer. No address residue (the trailing 'entry' is semantic, not a hex suffix). Consistent with sibling accessors in table.c (fd2_get_enemy_data_entry, fd2_get_char_base_entry).
purpose: Leaf accessor returning a byte pointer to the 2-byte class-promotion entry for a given promoted class id (class_id >= 0x20) in the read-only class-promotion data table at 0x615FE in .object3.
logic_summary: EAX = class_id (stack arg); EAX -= 0x20 (table starts at class 0x20); EAX <<= 1 (2-byte stride); EDX = 0x615FE (table base, via LEA); EAX += EDX; return EAX. No +1 baked into the result -- it returns the base of the 2-byte entry; callers index byte[0]/byte[1] themselves. The decompiler renders base 0x615FE as data_orphan_615fd + 1 (0x615FD + 1 = 0x615FE), which equals the same address as the LEA; the src form (table_base + (class_id-0x20)*2) is the correct interpretation.

params.name: class_id
params.semantics: Target/promoted class id, >= 0x20. Used as table index via (class_id - 0x20). In fd2_run_class_promotion_menu_main and fd2_render_promote_candidates_grid it is the chosen target class id; in fd2_execute_class_promotion_with_dialog the caller passes rt_chars[idx].bPortrait_id, which in the promotion context holds the new (promoted) class identity.
params.reason: Name accurately reflects the value's role as a class id used to index the promotion table; no address residue.

returns.semantics: Pointer to the base of the 2-byte entry &data_fd2_battle_class_promotion_data_table[(class_id-0x20)*2]. byte[0] = post-promotion job_id (00h..1Ah job-id space); byte[1] = learned-spell id on promotion (0 = none).

comment_original_issue: Original src comment was correct and precise (return value, exact assembly, 3 callers) but omitted the meaning of the 2 entry bytes, which is the key semantic of the returned pointer and explains callers indexing [0] (job_id) and [1] (spell_id).
notes: Cross-checked base address 0x615FE three ways: disassembly LEA [0x615fe], globals.h/btltab3.c symbol address, and decompiler data_orphan_615fd+1. Only xref to 0x615FE is the DATA ref from this accessor at 0x4e498 (no write-xref), confirming const correctness. Raw table bytes at 0x615FE match btltab3.c definition exactly. All 3 callers confirm byte[0]=job_id (rt_chars[idx].bJob_id = *promo_entry) and byte[1]=spell_id (if (*(promo_entry+1) != 0) -> learned spell).
